blocks.title: Circular Buffer & BufferNa Synchronization Flow
blocks.caption: BufferNa uses waitNotFull(size) and waitNotEmpty(0) for capacity/item counting, plus mutex(1) to protect writePointer, readPointer, and elements[].
blocks.source:
graph LR
  Prod["Producer: put(item)"] --> WNF["waitNotFull.acquire()"]
  WNF --> M1["mutex.acquire()"]
  M1 --> Write["elements[writePointer] = item\nwritePointer = (writePointer + 1) % size"]
  Write --> R1["waitNotEmpty.release()"]
  R1 --> U1["mutex.release()"]

  Cons["Consumer: get()"] --> WNE["waitNotEmpty.acquire()"]
  WNE --> M2["mutex.acquire()"]
  M2 --> Read["item = elements[readPointer]\nreadPointer = (readPointer + 1) % size"]
  Read --> R2["waitNotFull.release()"]
  R2 --> U2["mutex.release()"]
  classDef sem fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4f46e5,stroke-width:1.5px;
  class WNF,M1,R1,U1,WNE,M2,R2,U2 sem;

blocks.title: BufferNa (3 Semaphores) vs. BufferN (Passing the Baton)

annotations.note: Notice: after waitProd.acquire(), the woken producer does NOT re-acquire mutex—ownership was passed to it!
If a consumer is waiting, we release waitConso instead of mutex, transferring the critical section directly ('passage de témoin').

blocks.title: Critical Analysis: Exercises 1 & 2 (Slides 27–29)
blocks.content:
* **Exercise 1 — Can we swap `waitNotEmpty.release()` and `mutex.release()` in `BufferNa`?**
  **Yes!** Releasing `mutex` *before* `waitNotEmpty.release()` is actually **slightly better**: if a consumer wakes up immediately on `waitNotEmpty.release()`, `mutex` is already free so the consumer won't immediately block on `mutex.acquire()`. (Whereas acquiring `waitNotFull` and `mutex` at the *start* must NOT be swapped—that would deadlock!)
* **Exercise 2 — Can we split `mutex` into two semaphores (`mutexProd` and `mutexConso`)?**
  * **In `BufferNa`:** **Yes!** Producers only modify `writePointer` and consumers only modify `readPointer`, and `waitNotFull`/`waitNotEmpty` guarantee they never access the same slot simultaneously.
  * **In `BufferN` (optimized):** **No!** Both producers and consumers read and modify the shared `nbElements`, `nbWaitingProd`, and `nbWaitingConso` variables—they *must* share a single `mutex`.

blocks.question: Can we replace the single `mutex` in `BufferNa` and `BufferN` with two separate semaphores (`mutexProd` for producers and `mutexConso` for consumers)?
options: Yes in `BufferNa` (separate `writePointer` and `readPointer`), but NO in `BufferN` (both share `nbElements`, `nbWaitingProd`, and `nbWaitingConso`).
blocks.correct_answer: Yes in `BufferNa` (separate `writePointer` and `readPointer`), but NO in `BufferN` (both share `nbElements`, `nbWaitingProd`, and `nbWaitingConso`).
blocks.explanation: In `BufferNa`, `waitNotFull` and `waitNotEmpty` ensure producers and consumers never touch the same array slot simultaneously, and `writePointer`/`readPointer` are disjoint. In `BufferN`, both roles mutate `nbElements`, `nbWaitingProd`, and `nbWaitingConso`, requiring a single shared `mutex`.
